pages.hook: Birthdays and holidays are big moments in the USA. Learn how to say the date, because in the USA the month comes first.

facts.label: Month first
facts.sub: In the USA, 7/4 means July 4. In Brazil, 7/4 means April 7.

facts.label: Independence Day
facts.sub: The Declaration of Independence was adopted on July 4, 1776. People have fireworks and picnics.

facts.label: Birthday cake
facts.sub: People sing “Happy Birthday to You”, then blow out the candles.

facts.label: The Statue of Liberty
facts.sub: A gift from France, dedicated in New York.

pages.polite: Say **Happy birthday!** and add the person’s name. Say dates with ordinal numbers: “March tenth.”

mythfact.s: In the USA, 10/3 usually means October 3.
mythfact.why: The USA writes month/day. Many other countries write day/month.

mythfact.s: Independence Day in the USA is in December.
mythfact.why: It is on July 4.

mythfact.s: The Statue of Liberty was a gift from France.
mythfact.why: France gave it to the USA. It was dedicated in 1886.

mythfact.s: People often blow out candles on a birthday cake.
mythfact.why: They also make a wish before they blow.

mythfact.s: July fourth is called “Thanksgiving”.
mythfact.why: July 4 is Independence Day. Thanksgiving is in November.

lines: Bring a friend. We’ll have cake!

decode.q: What day and month is the party?

lines: No mail today. Parade at 10 a.m.

compare.br: In Brazil, Independence Day is September 7, and you write dates as day/month, like 10/03 for March 10.
compare.us: In the USA, Independence Day is July 4, and you write month/day, like 3/10 for March 10.
compare.tip: To avoid confusion, write the month in letters: March 10, not 3/10.
compare.ask: When is your birthday? Say the month and the day in English.

quiz.q: How do you answer “When is your birthday?”
What do you say to someone on a birthday?
quiz.why: Happy birthday! is the set phrase.

pages.title: Reading quest — A birthday on the Fourth of July · part 1
text: Dear diary, today is a special day. My friend Evan lives in **Detroit**, and his birthday is on July fourth. It is also Independence Day!
This morning I asked him, “**What’s the date today?**” He laughed. “**I forgot**!” he said. “Today is my birthday!” I said, “**Happy birthday**! **Make a wish**!”

We went to a park. Many people had picnics, and children had flags. I thought about the Statue of Liberty in New York. France gave it to the United States, and people dedicated it on October 28, 1886. It is a famous symbol of freedom, and many visitors take photos of it every day.

fast.why: Evan’s birthday is on July 4, Independence Day.

At night we saw fireworks over the river. Evan blew out the candles on his cake. It was the **best day ever**.

text: Dear diary, today is a special day. My friend Evan lives in **Detroit**, and his birthday is on July fourth. It is also Independence Day!
This morning I asked him, “**What’s the date today?**” He laughed. “**I forgot**!” he said. “Today is my birthday!” I said, “**Happy birthday**! **Make a wish**!”

We went to a park. Many people had picnics, and children had flags. I thought about the Statue of Liberty in New York. France gave it to the United States, and people dedicated it on October 28, 1886. It is a famous symbol of freedom, and many visitors take photos of it every day.

My birthday is in March, on March tenth. Evan said, “Let’s have a party **on a holiday** next year!” “It’s a date,” I said. We both laughed. In the USA, the month comes first, so I write 3/10 for my birthday. My friends say that is easy to remember, and I smile.
At night we saw fireworks over the river. Evan blew out the candles on his cake. It was the **best day ever**.

fast.why: Evan’s birthday is on July 4, Independence Day.
